definitions.explanation: A hall or space for practicing martial arts, traditional arts, or spiritual disciplines. Also used figuratively for any place of serious training or learning.

examples.japanese: {道場|どうじょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{稽古|けいこ}→稽古：00210_keiko⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{剣道|けんどう}→剣道：04452_kendou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{道場|どうじょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}いている→開く：01979_hiraku⟧。
examples.english: My father runs a kendo dojo.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{近所|きんじょ}→近所：01318_kinjo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{柔道|じゅうどう}→柔道：01612_juudou⟧{道場|どうじょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{通|かよ}い→通う：01217_kayou⟧、⟦{礼儀|れいぎ}→礼儀：03780_reigi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}んだ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
examples.english: Since childhood, I attended the local judo dojo and learned manners and technique.

notes:
Literally "place of the way" (⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧ + {場|じょう}). Originally a Buddhist term for a place of practice, it became associated with martial arts training halls.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {道場|どうじょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{通|かよ}う→通う：01217_kayou⟧ (attend a dojo)
- {道場|どうじょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}く→開く：01979_hiraku⟧ (open a dojo)
- {道場|どうじょう}{破|やぶ}り (challenging a dojo — showing up to fight its members)
- {道場|どうじょう}⟦{主|ぬし}→主：30578_nushi⟧ (dojo master/owner)

The word has been borrowed into English as "dojo." It is used for ⟦{剣道|けんどう}→剣道：04452_kendou⟧, ⟦{柔道|じゅうどう}→柔道：01612_juudou⟧, ⟦{空手|からて}→空手：04454_karate⟧, ⟦{合気道|あいきどう}→合気道：17630_aikidou⟧, and other martial arts. Figuratively, places of rigorous training in cooking, comedy, or other fields may be called {道場|どうじょう}. Not to be confused with the homophone ⟦{同情|どうじょう}→同情：11954_doujou⟧ (sympathy).
